questions.q: What is CSDM, fundamentally, according to this lesson?
options: ServiceNow's published, vendor-maintained reference framework for structuring CMDB, application, and service data consistently
A ServiceNow feature enabled with a single configuration toggle
A replacement for the CMDB that removes the need for CIs
A reporting dashboard that visualizes CI health
questions.explain: CSDM is documentation and a recommended structure to follow, not a toggle, dashboard, or CMDB replacement.

questions.q: Before CSDM was published as a standard, what was the real problem across modules like ITSM, ITOM, and Service Portfolio Management?
options: ServiceNow modules could not access the CMDB at all
There was no problem — the modules always agreed on structure
Each module and each implementation modeled services and applications inconsistently, with no shared structure
CIs could not be created until CSDM existed
questions.explain: Different modules and implementation teams grew their own expectations for service/application data, with nothing forcing a shared shape.

questions.q: What specific cost did that modeling inconsistency impose inside a single instance?
options: The instance would stop accepting new Incidents
Relationships between CIs became technically impossible to create
CIs would automatically delete themselves
Dashboards or reports built for one module could misread or simply fail to find records intended for another
questions.explain: When different modules expect data shaped differently, tools built against one module's expectations can miss records meant for another.

questions.q: What cost did that inconsistency impose across different customers and implementation teams?
options: Every implementation re-derived its own structure from scratch, so lessons learned rarely transferred between engagements
Service Portfolio Management was removed from the product entirely
Customers were charged additional licensing fees for each module
Nothing — inconsistency across customers carried no real cost
questions.explain: Without a shared standard, every implementation partner started from zero, and admins had to relearn a bespoke model at every new job or client.

questions.q: What does CSDM give implementers, per this lesson?
options: A guarantee that no further configuration work is ever needed
A way to skip modeling Business Services entirely
Automatic, zero-effort Discovery of every CI in the environment
A documented, well-tested starting structure instead of a blank page
questions.explain: CSDM documents what a correct structure looks like, so implementers don't have to invent one independently each time.
